relations.note: Johnson cautiously calls Moremi probably his wife; later Ifẹ̀ tradition makes the marriage definite.
He is Moremi's only son, named variously Elà, Olúorogbo, or both.
Moremi yields her son as the demanded sacrifice; Johnson says he dies and joins the gods.

relations.myth: Ela revives and ascends to heaven
relations.note: In Ogumefu's variant, her sacrificed son revives, climbs heavenward, and promises to return.

relations.myth: Moremi's vow before infiltrating the raiders
relations.note: The river power grants or enables Moremi's success after receiving her vow.

relations.myth: Payment of the promised river offering
relations.note: After rejecting animal substitutes, the river power receives Moremi's only son as her promised offering.
Blier reconstructs Moremi's captors and opponents as forces associated with Obalufon and the earlier population.
Later harmonized genealogy makes him Moremi's father-in-law through her marriage to his son Ọ̀rànmíyàn.
Beier makes Moremi's sacrifice reconcile Odùduwà's polity with the spirits of displaced landowners.
